title: Plumas Working Forests — method costs, harvest baseline, and gaps
disclaimer: Absolute figures are the best public / published numbers we can cite. Confidence: A=official CA schedule or county harvest series; B=published regional industry study (not a live Plumas bid); C=illustrative; D=gap (null). Wholesale chain uses Tahoe-Central Sierra / French Meadows delivered-log and logging schedules (MB&G 2020) — Sierra-adjacent, not Plumas-confidential contracts. Net owner profit still requires local haul distance + actual mill quotes. Do not invent; fill via program/data/INTAKE.md.

confidence_legend.A: Official California schedule or published county harvest series with stable methodology
confidence_legend.B: Peer-reviewed or multi-study Western US / CA range; not Plumas-bid-specific
confidence_legend.C: Illustrative / order-of-magnitude only — not for business decisions
confidence_legend.D: Data gap — value is null or intentionally omitted

geography.tva_note: CDTFA Timber Value Areas follow county lines (with I-5 splits in Shasta/Siskiyou/Tehama). Plumas sits in the interior Sierra TVA band; cite the TVA column used when applying Table G.

plumas_harvest_mbf.source: University of Montana BBER Forest Industry Research — Timber Harvest for Plumas County, California
plumas_harvest_mbf.notes: Private includes industrial + NIPF + tribal where reported; FS = USDA Forest Service. Post-Dixie years (2021–2023) show elevated private salvage/green volume — not a steady-state baseline alone.

stumpage_cdtfa_ihv.source: CDTFA Harvest Values Schedule (Table G green timber), effective 2026-01-01 through 2026-06-30
stumpage_cdtfa_ihv.unit: USD per MBF (immediate harvest value for yield tax — not the same as every private stumpage contract)
stumpage_cdtfa_ihv.notes: Table values assume tractor logging and ≥300 MBF quarter volume. Skyline −$100/MBF; helicopter −$350/MBF; small total volume and low volume/acre deductions apply. Biomass/chips (Table 1 CS) IHV = $0/ton.

industry_layers.note: Value chain from stump to wholesale fiber. Stumpage residual = delivered price - stump-to-truck logging - haul (- chip for biomass).
industry_layers.equation: Stumpage = DeliveredPrice - LoggingCost - HaulCost [- ChipCost for biomass]

layers.name: Standing timber value (tax IHV / residual stumpage)
layers.what_it_is: What the tree is worth on the stump after logging and haul are paid — residual to landowner (or bid on public sales). CDTFA IHV is a tax schedule proxy, not every private contract.

layers.name: Stump-to-truck logging (cut, yard, process, load)
layers.what_it_is: Logger / LTO production cost to put logs on a truck at the landing.

layers.name: Haul (landing to mill or biomass plant)
layers.what_it_is: Truck cost; two-way time + load/unload. Dominates biomass economics at long distance.

layers.name: Delivered log price (mill gate / pond value)
layers.what_it_is: What the mill pays for logs delivered — the wholesale wood fiber price for sawtimber sorts.

layers.name: Biomass / chip delivered (plant gate)
layers.what_it_is: Delivered price for energy/chip fiber. Often too low to cover logging+chip+haul → negative biomass stumpage.

layers.name: Mill output lumber wholesale
layers.what_it_is: Random Lengths-style lumber selling prices. Gap for live series in this ledger — mill margin = lumber - log - mill conversion.

layers.name: Reforestation & free-to-grow (plant + release)
layers.what_it_is: Post-harvest costs that do not show in log wholesale but drive the clearcut+spray pathway economics.

delivered_log_tcsi.label: Delivered log prices — Lake Tahoe / Central Sierra region (study assumptions)
delivered_log_tcsi.source: Mason, Bruce & Girard / TNC Tahoe-Central Sierra Initiative Phase 1 Restoration Wood Supply Assessment (Dec 2020), Table 13; prices from confidential contemporary log prices / French Meadows Project (TNC 2018)
delivered_log_tcsi.year_context: Study published 2020; log prices referenced as contemporary ~2018 French Meadows / regional confidential
delivered_log_tcsi.notes: Same $/MBF across SED classes in the published table (study simplification). Not a 2026 live quote; use as Sierra wholesale order-of-magnitude until mill interviews.

logging_sawtimber_tcsi_table.label: Sawtimber stump-to-truck logging cost by removal intensity and system (Sierra study)
logging_sawtimber_tcsi_table.source: MB&G TCSI Phase 1 (2020) Table 14; MB&G regional data / French Meadows Project (Robert Galliano pers. comm.)
logging_sawtimber_tcsi_table.notes: Low volume/acre thins cost more per MBF. Cable always above tractor. Maps cleanly to Working Forest (often 3–14 MBF/ac) vs heavy regen harvest (20–40+ MBF/ac).

haul_tcsi.label: Haul cost parameters (Sierra study)
haul_tcsi.source: MB&G TCSI Phase 1 (2020); Mason Bruce & Girard and The Beck Group High Hazard Fuel Availability Study 2019
haul_tcsi.notes: Haul is two-way (empty return). $/MBF = (2 * one_way_hours + idle) * 88 / 4.97. Example: 1.5 hr one-way → (3+0.75)*88/4.97 ≈ \/MBF.

biomass_tcsi.label: Biomass logging, chip, delivered price (Sierra study)
biomass_tcsi.source: MB&G TCSI Phase 1 (2020); High Hazard Fuel Study 2019
biomass_tcsi.notes: Stumpage residual ≈ 40 - 13 - 20 - haul. Haul alone often exceeds residual → negative biomass stumpage (study found Rocklin haul distances generally too long for positive biomass stumpage at \/BDT). CDTFA tax IHV for chips/biomass = \/ton.

thin_stump_to_truck_chang.label: Western US thinning stump-to-truck by system (literature synthesis)
thin_stump_to_truck_chang.source: Chang et al. 2023, Journal of Forestry — systematic review of Western US thinning costs
thin_stump_to_truck_chang.year_context: Review of 1980–2020 studies; costs in paper as reported (not all inflated to 2026)
thin_stump_to_truck_chang.notes: Cheapest common system: feller-buncher + skidder + processor + loader ~\/ton stump-to-truck. Cable systems exceed ~\/ton. Complements TCSI \$/MBF table (different units).

regional_mill_capacity_tcsi.label: Regional mill capacity near Sierra core (for offtake context)
regional_mill_capacity_tcsi.source: MB&G TCSI Phase 1 (2020) Table 9 — Beck Group capacity summary
regional_mill_capacity_tcsi.year_context: As of study (~2019–2020); facilities change — verify current
regional_mill_capacity_tcsi.notes: SPI Quincy is the Plumas-adjacent sawmill. Capacities are study-era consumption estimates.
